title: Africa's $124 Billion in Remittances: Who Receives It and What It Costs to Send | The Six, Ep. 7
lede: Migrants and the diaspora sent an estimated $124.2 billion home to Africa in 2025, almost twice the continent's foreign direct investment. This episode looks at where the money goes, why Sub-Saharan Africa is the most expensive region to send to, and the new U.S. tax on cash-funded transfers.
keyPoints: Remittances to Africa reached an estimated $124.2 billion in 2025, up 86% since 2016 (IFAD, Sending Money Home 2026). FDI into Africa was about $70 billion (UNCTAD).
Egypt ($41.5bn), Nigeria ($22.8bn), Morocco ($13.7bn), Ethiopia ($7.1bn) and Kenya ($5.0bn) received about 73% of the total. Egypt's central bank reports a record $47.3bn for the year to June 2026.
Remittances equal about a fifth of GDP in The Gambia, Liberia, Comoros and Lesotho (IFAD).

Sending $200 to Sub-Saharan Africa cost 8.46% on average in Q3 2025, against a 6.36% global average and a UN target under 3% (World Bank). Fully digital services averaged about 4.6%, cash-based ones 7.3% (IFAD).
Since Jan. 1, 2026 the U.S. taxes cash-, money order- and cashier's check-funded remittances at 1%; IRS rules are still at the proposed stage.
